finalText:
**What happened:** Redis went down at 2:14 AM, and the app never recovered from it.

1. At 02:14:07 the connection to redis (10.0.0.12:6379) dropped. The app fell back to hitting the database directly instead of the cache.
2. That fallback couldn't keep up. Requests started timing out every few seconds, and the backlog of waiting requests grew nonstop for the next 17 minutes, from 52 up to over 560.
3. Redis reconnect attempts kept firing roughly every 80 seconds and kept failing, all the way to attempt 12 at 02:31:26 — redis simply never came back.
4. At 02:31:44 one of the workers ran out of memory from the backlog and crashed.
5. Eight seconds later, at 02:31:52, the supervisor gave up and killed the whole process group — that's the outage.

So the root cause is redis becoming unreachable and staying that way; everything else (timeouts, growing queue, out-of-memory crash) was downstream of that one failure. The fix that matters most is getting redis back and keeping the app from piling up unbounded work when its cache is gone — a queue cap or circuit breaker would have kept this from turning into a full crash. Worth checking why `10.0.0.12:6379` was unreachable for 17+ straight minutes.
